name: GLM-5.2
tagline: A million tokens of context under plain MIT
description: Z.ai's 753B-total / ~40B-active MoE flagship with a 1M-token context window and IndexShare attention that cuts per-token FLOPs 2.9× at full length. Ships in BF16 and FP8 on Hugging Face with day-0 vLLM and SGLang support, plus llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio quantizations.
why: The long-horizon workhorse of this summer's open-weights wave — MIT weights with no rider, no territory clause, no MAU cap. Already the engine behind community projects like Colibri, which streams its experts off disk to run it in ~25GB of RAM.
useCases: Long-document analysis and sustained agentic sessions
audience: Infra-rich teams; determined locals via community quantizations

setup.requirements: Multi-GPU node for BF16/FP8; community GGUF routes (see Colibri) trade latency for ~25GB-RAM consumer setups

license.notes: Weights carry a plain MIT tag on Hugging Face. At check time the GLM-5 GitHub repo documented GLM-5/5.1 only — the 5.2 release lives on Hugging Face, so verify the license of the exact checkpoint you pull.

limitations: MoE inference at this scale is hardware-hungry, several hosts cap context well below 1M, and Z.ai's launch benchmark suite was thin — independent verification is still filling in.
take: Colibri proved people will stream experts off a hard drive to run this model. A clean MIT license is why they bother.
